properties.baseline_note:
PRUNED 2026-09-22, the same day it was set, from 220 to 184. Nothing was excused: `link_artifact` was fixed to draw IMPLEMENTS for a Verification target (it had drawn REALIZES, which the schema's own hint calls the wrong edge for that pair), and the 46 links it had drawn in error across 40 checks were migrated. 36 grandfathered capabilities turned out to have had a runnable check all along — the edge recording it was the thing missing, not the test. Executable forms went 30 -> 71, capabilities verified by a runnable check 22 -> 58, and the population of checks with a registered file and no form went 40 -> 0.

ORIGINALLY, 2026-09-22: computed from docs/design/reflow2.json at the merge-base with main. Capabilities carrying at least one passing VERIFIES whose Verification has zero incoming IMPLEMENTS. 220 of 291.

The set may shrink and may never grow. A prune is the shrink working; the gate names the candidates and the judgement stays here.
properties.decision: From 2026-09-22, a capability whose only passing Verification has no executable form — nothing IMPLEMENTS it — is a build failure. The 220 capabilities already in that state on this date are grandfathered by id in `baseline_ids` and the bar ratchets from there: the set may shrink and may never grow. This does NOT require a new capability to carry a check. A capability with no check at all is unverified and honest, and capture-intent must stay free to record intent before anything is built. What is forbidden is the CLAIM: asserting a passing check that nothing can re-run.
properties.name: A capability may not NEWLY reach verified on a claim nothing can re-run
properties.rationale:
MEASURED on this design 2026-09-22, off the committed export: 291 capabilities, 241 verified by their own passing check — and only 21 of those by a check anything implements. 220 rest on a claim. Of 312 Verifications, 311 read `passing` and 30 have an executable form. The coverage line said '241/288 capability(ies) verified' and a reader met it as a thoroughly verified design.

The code underneath was genuinely at 85.47% region / 87.17% line coverage. The TESTS are real; the RECORD of them was not, and that gap is the half of an outside reader's 'this sounds like an AI coding project' that actually lands.

WHY A SET AND NOT A COUNT — the same argument `check_intent_authority.py` records for its own grandfathered set. Counting claim-only capabilities and failing above a baseline is smaller and wrong: implement a check for one old capability and introduce one new claim, and the count is unchanged, so the gate passes while the thing it exists to catch has happened.

WHY THE SET LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE TOOL — likewise from the precedent: which capabilities were already claim-only is a fact about the design and belongs in the design, and a list living in tools/ could be edited to silence a finding without that edit ever surfacing in a design review.

WHY NOT BACKFILL THE 220 — the same ruling Anthony gave on the authority check: grandfather it, guard forward, do not backfill. Writing 220 tests to make a number green is the behaviour the number exists to detect.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: it does not judge whether a check is any good. `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` stands untouched. It reports a fact the graph already holds — the same signal `has_executable_form` has carried in the loop digest all along — and refuses to let that fact get worse.

HONEST LIMITS. (1) The exemption does not expire: a grandfathered capability that earns a runnable check and later loses it re-enters the claim-only set silently, because it is still on the list. The gate prints the earned ones and asks for them to be pruned; nothing forces it. (2) An IMPLEMENTS edge only says a file was named, never that the file runs or that the run is the one recorded — `reconcile_verification` is the instrument for that, and it is a different question.

Anthony's word, 2026-09-22: 'go with your recommendation for how to test. We can revisit stop-the-build if that is wrong', and then 'Go with your recommendations and ordering'.
